cut fetches the target branch from origin and prepares the release from its
tip in a scratch checkout: it resolves the version, authors and renders the
changelog, writes it into CHANGELOG.md, runs commands.propagate to write the
version into the manifests (with RELEASE_VERSION set), refuses a change to
any path that is neither CHANGELOG.md nor in release_paths, and runs
commands.validate. Only then does it write: it creates the stage branch at
the fetched tip, commits the release as "Release <version>", pushes the
branch to origin, and opens a pull request into the target with gh. Your
working tree, index and current branch are never read or changed.

bump is major, minor or patch, and names the impact instead of inferring
it. A named bump is refused when the commits since the base version indicate
no bump (there are none, or none is releasable), unless --force is given.
When standard input is a terminal, cut shows the writes it will make and
asks once before the first. It never tags, publishes, merges, or changes the
target branch. Exits 1 when it refuses (nothing to release, an impact
disagreement, an existing stage branch, a failing configured command, a
path outside release_paths), having written nothing, and 3 when a write
failed after another succeeded, having reported every write it made. If the
push fails, cut deletes the local stage branch it created.

Usage:
  release cut [bump] [flags]

Flags:
      --dry-run           Report every intended action and change nothing
      --force             Cut the named bump even when nothing releasable exists since the base version. Requires bump
  -h, --help              help for cut
      --json              Render the answer as JSON instead of YAML
      --no-pull-request   Create and push the stage branch and stop; open no pull request
      --redo-notes        Discard any cached corpus and author again
      --skip-notes        Stage without an authoring exchange. Requires bump
      --target branch     The release line to cut from: a branch on origin (default: the configured target, else the branch origin/HEAD points to)
      --yes               Do not prompt before writing. Only meaningful interactively

Global Flags:
      --config file   Use this configuration file instead of discovering one
  -C, --repo path     Operate on the repository at this path instead of the working directory
